frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:394-411 — the mount-time initializeAuth effect duplicates token-refresh logic inline (calls getAuthApi().refreshToken() directly) instead of delegating to refreshTokenInternal (AuthContext.tsx:346-383). The inline path sets the new access/refresh tokens but SKIPS the deriveActiveRole re-derivation that refreshTokenInternal performs (AuthContext.tsx:366-374, the #574 multi-tenant fix). Result: on a cold app boot where the access token is absent/expired but a refresh token is present, the user's stored role is NOT re-derived from the fresh JWT — a multi-tenant user whose active tenant/role changed server-side boots with a STALE role (falls into the if (storedUser) setUser(storedUser) branch at line 408-410 using the old persisted role) until a later refreshTokenInternal call corrects it. The #574 fix is therefore incomplete on the init path. The inline path also bypasses the single-flight refresh guard (isRefreshing/refreshPromise). Fix: have initializeAuth call refreshTokenInternal() in the refresh branch so role derivation + concurrency guard apply uniformly.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:246-259 — the auth-change effect re-runs on [auth.isAuthenticated, auth.accessToken] and calls service.connect() whenever the access token changes. But WebSocketService.connect() (lib/websocket.ts) short-circuits with 'if (this.socket && this.socket.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) return; // Already connected'. AuthContext rotates BOTH tokens on every refresh (refreshTokenInternal sets a new accessToken, AuthContext.tsx:356), so on a normal token rotation the effect fires while the socket is still OPEN and connect() returns early — the live WebSocket is NEVER re-handshaked with the fresh token.

The JWT is transmitted only as the ?token=<jwt> handshake query param (lib/websocket.ts:88-94, buildWebSocketUrl) and validated by api-server once at connection time. Consequently a long-lived WS connection keeps running under the ORIGINAL access token past its TTL. Two failure modes: (a) if api-server enforces token expiry mid-connection the socket is dropped and auto-reconnect recovers, causing avoidable drop/reconnect churn plus a window where events flow on an expired token; (b) if the server does not re-validate mid-connection, a session whose token was rotated/revoked (e.g. logout-elsewhere) keeps receiving realtime push data because the WS was never re-authenticated. Fix: when the token changes and a socket is already open, force a reconnect (disconnect()+connect(), or a dedicated re-auth) rather than relying on connect()'s already-open early-return. Confidence medium: severity of (b) depends on reality/api-server WS TTL enforcement, not traced in this static frontend slice.
